conditions: n is a nonnegative integer; n independent Bernoulli trials have identical success probability p with 0<p<1; k is an integer satisfying 0<=k<=n.
spoken_aliases: the probability that random variable x equals k equals n choose k times p to the power k times open parenthesis one minus p close parenthesis raised to the power of open parenthesis n minus k close parenthesis

the probability that x equals k equals the product of the binomial coefficient n choose k and p raised to the power k and the quantity one minus p raised to the power of the quantity n minus k end exponent

evidence: Each ordered sequence containing k successes and n-k failures has probability p^k(1-p)^(n-k) by independence. Exactly C(n,k) mutually exclusive sequences have that success count. Summing their probabilities gives the formula. The binomial theorem shows the probabilities sum to one.
